title: DesignChoices 2.0: reasoned starting values for parameters no evidence sets directly
description: A process needs every physical setpoint to have a number before anyone can run it, and the literature rarely reports the one for this exact process. A design choice is the honest third option between a cited value and a blocking gap: a number proposed by reasoning from adjacent practice, with what it was derived from, how sure its author is, and what would settle it. It is never a reported value, it never becomes evidence, and a human approves it before the wet lab -- which is the same rule a ProductionProtocol already applies to its own design_choice provenance. A value that must not be guessed stays a gap.

rationale.description: Why this number: the reasoning from what is known to what is proposed

derived_from.description: What it was reasoned from: claim ids, PMIDs, a named practice, a related cell type or format. 'Common practice' alone is a weak but statable basis; an empty list is not.

context_note.description: How the source context differs from this process

would_settle_it.description: The measurement or source that would replace this guess with a value
